name: github

verification.follow_up: Ratify and run the independent connector evidence contract.

_error_map_note: Reference: GitHub REST API 'Troubleshooting the REST API' + 'Authenticating to the REST API' (docs.github.com/rest). GitHub emits NO numeric error code -- its whole error vocabulary is the body's 'message' string: {"message": "Bad credentials", "documentation_url": "...", "status": "401"}. core.pull_errors._extract_provider_codes reads no 'message' field, so connector._github_error_payload() surfaces that exact string at the top-level 'reason' slot (the shape core consults first among top-level keys) while keeping every original key as evidence -- the stripe/square normalisation pattern, never provider vocabulary inside core. KEYS ARE THEREFORE THE VERBATIM DOCUMENTED MESSAGES. '401:Bad credentials' is auth_revoked, not auth_expired: the connector presents a user-supplied PAT verbatim (no refresh flow), so a rejected credential is one GitHub no longer holds -- deleted, rotated or revoked by secret scanning -- and the repair is to supply a new token, not to wait for a refresh. '404:Not Found' is permission_denied and is the entry that matters most: GitHub deliberately answers 404 instead of 403 for a private repository the token cannot see, so that a probe cannot learn the repository exists; without this key core leaves it 'unclassified', i.e. retried forever with nothing to tell the operator. NO 403 KEY IS DECLARED, and that is deliberate: _pull_releases/_pull_deployments still raise a raw PermissionError on 403 before classify_http_error is reached (GitHub returns 403, not 429, on the primary rate limit, and splitting the two needs header inspection), so a 403 key would be a dead key -- the exact defect AI-114 removed elsewhere. Re-open it with the 403 refactor. 429 keeps the core.quota.RateLimitError breaker path and is never keyed here.
_account_topology_note: Token-scoped context source: one PAT or OAuth token addresses exactly one repository (owner+repo stored in Nango connection metadata). No account discovery hierarchy exists -- the repository itself is the root scope. account_topology is not declared.
_max_provider_backfill_days_note: No max_provider_backfill_days is declared: this provider's published reporting window has not been established as of 2026-08-17. The key is left absent rather than filled with an estimate -- an invented re-collection bound promises the operator a history the provider never committed to. Establishing it means reading the provider's own documentation and recording the URL here, as the modules that do declare one have done.
